subtitle: A dreamer enters a land without dreams

body: Klonoa: Empire of Dreams is Now Production's Game Boy Advance puzzle platformer placing the long-eared traveller in the Empire of Jillius, where dreaming has been forbidden. His journey uses compact two-dimensional stages built around catching and throwing enemies with the Wind Ring. The portable adventure gives the familiar character a more enclosed kind of challenge, with each room asking how its creatures and movable objects can help reach the necessary stars. Progress comes from understanding what can be carried and where that temporary resource needs to be used.

The Wind Ring draws a nearby enemy into Klonoa's grasp. From there, he can throw it toward another target or use it to perform a double jump, exchanging the carried creature for additional height. Large blocks can also be picked up and positioned to change a route. The same object can therefore have several possible purposes, and choosing one may remove another option. A successful sequence depends on keeping the useful resource available until the point where its throw, weight or contribution to a jump is actually required.

Each stage requires three stars before its exit can be used, giving the small spaces a clear structure beyond simply moving toward the right edge of the screen. Optional crystals and hidden rewards invite a closer reading of the same arrangement. Klonoa can also briefly hover by flapping his ears, providing a little more control after leaving the ground. The combination allows a short stage to contain a careful sequence of decisions, where an apparently unreachable star becomes accessible once the correct enemy or block has been brought into position.
